correctness.rationale: For every real d>=1, c*d*d<b implies the exact two-step return is uniformly Lipschitz with constant <1. All branch and endpoint cases are addressed. For a>b this gives a unique globally attracting two-cycle and uniqueness among all invariant Borel probabilities by Cesaro limits. For a=b the continuous return extension fixes zero, but the actual map has 0->b->1->c; all real trajectories have omega={0,b}, whose empirical measure is non-invariant. An invariant probability would have to equal this empirical limit by dominated convergence, a contradiction. The weak-limit and d>1 scaling follow from the fixed-point inequality and chain rule. Representative exact rational checks corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The base model was designed to exhibit dynamics without equilibria, so its stationary statistical dynamics and recurrence at a boundary are central natural questions. An open contraction region suffers total loss of invariant Borel measures even as all trajectories remain bounded and empirical measures converge, while the maps and their unique stationary states converge. The exact d-dependent cycle amplitude and multiplier exponents identify a distinctive superattracting-to-ghost mechanism that is not implied by general existence counterexamples. The contraction assumption is explicit and sufficient, not falsely promoted as a sharp general frontier.
